items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: With Dick Hyman, it’s unpredictable... I know you’ve been playing with both Dick Hyman and with Peter Duchin.

ctx.x: So it’s almost like playing a Broadway show, where you do one thing. You’ve got the order down.

Yeah. It’s sort of an order. We don’t always play them in the same order, but we play basically the same music all the time. With Dick Hyman, it’s unpredictable. You don’t know what Dick is going to write. Dick can come up with some very complicated things. He multi-talented and has an inexhaustible source of energy, and he’s very creative. As I say, with Dick you don’t know what you are going to play when he shows up. That’s challenging. That’s nice. It puts you to the test. And he has a great – he’s very loyal,…
Yeah. I know what you’re talking about. If you were to talk to someone who was getting started in music today, what would you want to say to them in terms of what a life in music is like?

items.title: Joe Wilder Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: there is also one I did with Dick Hyman

ctx.x: What are some of the things you’ve been doing? I know we have one of your recent records here and —
Well that’s the most recent one, and there is also one I did with Dick Hyman, the name of which I don’t remember, but it’s a recent one also. But this is the last one I have.
In the past few years you’ve played with the Smithsonian —
